evidence: Message model (src/sqllens/agent/core/storage/models.py:17-28) has tool_calls: Optional[List[ToolCall]], provider_content: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]], tool_call_id: Optional[str], role str. ToolCall (agent/core/tool/models.py:23) has id: str. Agent.send_message builds assistant Message with tool_calls=response.tool_calls and provider_content=response.provider_content (agent.py:695-700), both Optional so possibly None; tool results saved as Message(role='tool', tool_call_id=...) (agent.py:1043-1047). query_database.py:227-261 handles None via 'or ()' and uses .id, role, tool_call_id consistently. Dict block .get used with isinstance guard.

llm.py:158-167 _build_payload: for an assistant message with provider_content not None, it deep-copies provider_content and appends it as the assistant message, then continues, without consulting m.tool_calls (tool_calls only read at line 200 in the else branch). Only thinking/redacted_thinking blocks from older turns are filtered (160-163), so tool_use blocks are kept; the message is dropped only if content is empty. So tool_use blocks reach the API even when tool_calls is empty.

Ordering holds: agent.py:695-701 does conversation.add_message(assistant tool_use) before the tool loop (738+), and tool messages are appended at 1042-1048 after all tools ran, in order, directly after the assistant message. But the agent does not SAVE at those points. conversation_store.update_conversation is called only at 351, 505, 526 (new-conversation/starter/workflow paths, before the user message) and 1185 (end of the whole send_message, after the loop). Between the tool_use append and the tool results there is no update_conversation call; add_message (models.py:45-48) only appends to the in-memory list. The persisted store sees the tool_use only because the built-in stores (local/storage.py:36-43, conversation_store.py:71-80) hand back the same live object; a store returning copies would not see it until the 1185 save, which a mid-tool failure skips. So the docstring's 'saves ... before its tools run and results after' is inaccurate as worded (it is an in-memory append, not a save), though the ordering it relies on is correct.

conversation_store.py:68-77 get_conversation returns the live stored Conversation object (same object the agent appends to) when the user id matches, so messages appended during the call are visible. conversation_store.py:98-139 truncate_messages(conversation_id, user_id, length) does `del conversation.messages[length:]`, dropping index length onward (no-op if length >= len; ValueError if negative; raises on owner mismatch). It is synchronous and query_database.py:311 calls it without await with (conversation_id, user.id, cut), matching the signature.

llm.py:72 sets self._client in __init__; send_request (llm.py:74-78) calls `await self._client.messages.create(**payload)` and the non-streaming path never touches client.messages.stream (only stream_request, llm.py:115). The test config sets stream_responses=False (line 155), so the non-streaming path is used.

agent.py:701 adds the assistant tool_use message before tool execution. agent.py:861 awaits self.tool_registry.execute with no enclosing try that handles it (the except at 513 belongs to the earlier workflow-handler block). The exception propagates to send_message (agent.py:174-225), which catches Exception and yields a StatusCardComponent(title='Error Processing Message', status='error') instead of raising. _format.py:434-497 turns a status='error' card into (error_message, True, ...). query_database.py:673-676 then raises AgentRunError with prefix 'SQL execution error: ' (_SQL_EXECUTION_ERROR_PREFIX, line 93). The test at tests/unit/test_query_database_tool_history.py:236-253 matches this chain.

In an armed call (armed after _seed, test line 351), reads of get_conversation occur in this order: (1) query_database.py:221 via _conversation_baseline, called at :578 before agent.send_message; (2) agent.py:431, the agent's own load in the normal send_message path (the only other get_conversation in agent.py is :301, the starter-UI branch, not taken); (3) query_database.py:283 in _trim_unanswered_tool_use, called at :596/:601 after send_message. Tool execute is mocked, so no other reads. The test's `reads >= 3` raising therefore hits the trim's read, and the logged breadcrumb 'raised from get_conversation' matches query_database.py:288.

query_database.py:276-280 docstring says _trim_unanswered_tool_use 'Never raises Exception' and that the caller's result must not be replaced by a cleanup failure. Only get_conversation (282-292) and truncate (310-321) are in try/except. Line 295 `_first_unanswered_tool_use(conversation.messages, start)` is unguarded, and it runs _tool_use_ids (227-238). Message.provider_content is typed Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] (agent/core/llm/models.py:26), so a schema-valid stored block {"type":"tool_use","id":["x"]} reaches `ids.add(block.get("id"))` at line 237 and raises TypeError (unhashable). A custom conversation store returning malformed messages (missing .role etc.) would also raise from lines 249-258. The exception propagates out of the trim, contradicting the absolute claim. Realistic Anthropic ids are strings, so reach is narrow, but the claim is absolute and the scan is outside any guard.

_first_unanswered_tool_use (query_database.py:241-261) iterates range(start, len(messages)), so it can only return an index >= start; the trim truncates to that index (line 311), so nothing below start is cut. start is the message count read by _conversation_baseline (208-224) after the per-conversation turn lock is taken (563-580), and the trim runs inside the same lock (596-603), so no other call on the same id appends in between. Absolute-claim input traced: the bounded store evicts the conversation mid-call (conversation_store.py:148-149) and the agent re-creates it with fewer messages. Old history is then gone, and scanning from start sees only indices >= start of the new list. If the new list is shorter than start, the range is empty and nothing is cut. Eviction cannot make the trim remove an earlier call's messages. The cost is that this call's own unanswered tool_use at an index below start would go unscanned, which is a different property from the one claimed.

Grep of src/ for truncate_messages finds only two invocations: query_database.py:311 inside _trim_unanswered_tool_use (def at 264) and query_database.py:366 inside _rollback_conversation (def at 330). Both are called from the query_database tool body (lines 596/601 and 612). The only other occurrences are the definition (conversation_store.py:98), docstrings and log text. Claim matches.

Inside the turn lock, _conversation_baseline (208-224) records the user and len(messages) before the agent run; the outer `except asyncio.CancelledError` (604-615) calls _rollback_conversation(agent, queued_id, baseline_user.id, baseline_messages) then re-raises. _rollback_conversation (330-413) calls the synchronous BoundedConversationStore.truncate_messages (conversation_store.py:98-143), which does `del conversation.messages[length:]` on the same Conversation object, so C is restored to exactly its pre-call messages (including the saved assistant tool_use). The lock is released only after the handler (context manager exit), so the next call sees the restored history. Test tests/unit/test_query_database_tool_history.py:216-233 uses the real Agent, BoundedConversationStore and a stub Anthropic client, cancels while run_sql is parked (assistant tool_use saved, no tool_result), asserts history == before, then next call returns 'Done.' and _assert_every_tool_use_answered passes on the recorded request (179-194). Trigger split: the code condition `baseline_user is not None and queued_id is not None` -> queued_id None (conversation_id None) -> outside the trigger (claim names a conversation C; the agent mints a private id unreachable by others, per 168-179); baseline_user None only if baseline read failed, which raises RuntimeError before the agent runs, so no tool_use is saved -> outside the trigger. Fault alternatives in _rollback_conversation (missing truncate_messages, ConversationOwnerMismatchError, other exception) -> outside the trigger: the claim fixes the store as BoundedConversationStore, whose method exists and raises only for negative length (impossible from len()) or an owner mismatch (not reachable with _StaticUserResolver); each logs at ERROR and does not displace the CancelledError. Rollback returning False (conversation evicted mid-call) -> nothing to restore, not a departure. Cancellation arriving during the post-run trim is caught by the same outer handler.

criteria.json is a valid list of {criterion,text} objects and carries criterion 2, which is this claim verbatim, so it counts. Traced head src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py. _tool_use_ids (227-238) collects ids from message.tool_calls and from provider_content tool_use blocks. _first_unanswered_tool_use (241-261) scans from `start` (the baseline message count taken under the turn lock, 208-224), skips non-assistant messages, and returns the index of the earliest assistant message whose ids are not all in the run of role=tool messages directly after it. _trim_unanswered_tool_use (264-327) calls store.truncate_messages(conversation_id, user.id, cut) with cut = that index. The cut is therefore at or after start+1, because the call's own user message sits at index start. Every earlier message, the call's user message included, stays. BoundedConversationStore.truncate_messages (conversation_store.py:98-143) does `del messages[length:]`. It logs logger.warning naming conversation_id and `removed` = len(messages) - cut (322-327), and only after a successful truncate. The call sites (589-603) run the trim on both the normal-return path and the `except Exception` path (before re-raise), inside the turn lock. The next call's Anthropic payload (agent/integrations/anthropic/llm.py:155-190) emits each tool_use followed by a grouped tool_result user message. After the trim no unmatched tool_use remains, so the next request is valid and succeeds. Tests in tests/unit/test_query_database_tool_history.py drive the real Agent with BoundedConversationStore and a recording stub client. test_error_answer_with_unanswered_tool_use_is_trimmed (240-265) asserts history == before + the user message, a WARNING containing conversation id and 'removed 1 message(s)', and a next call that returns Done. with every tool_use answered. The raising-send_message variant is at 268-292. Trigger split of the conditions that skip or alter the trim: (a) queued_id is None / baseline_user is None -> outside the trigger, because the claim is about a concrete conversation C, and None is reached only by a direct caller passing conversation_id=None, which mints a private id; (b) store.get_conversation raising, conversation None, or truncate_messages missing/raising -> outside the trigger by sibling criterion 5: 'When a trim is needed and the conversation store has no `truncate_messages`, or reading the conversation or calling `truncate_messages` raises, the call logs at ERROR...'. These fail loud at ERROR and return the call's own result. With the shipped BoundedConversationStore, none of them fires; (c) cut is None (no unanswered tool_use) -> outside the trigger, since no unanswered tool_use is the claim's precondition; (d) CancelledError -> outside the trigger, since the claim says 'without cancellation' and criterion 1 covers cancellation by full rollback. Non-Exception BaseExceptions are not named by the claim.
